# Filter

Source: https://github.com/ovidijusparsiunas/active-table/blob/main/website/docs/docs/filter.mdx

sidebar_position: 9

# Filter

Filter data inside the table.

### `filter` {#filterRows}

- Type: `boolean` | [`Filter`](#Filter) | [`Filter[]`](#Filter)

Generates an input component that can filter rows for a target column based on its value. This property can be set using
a `boolean`, a [`Filter`](#Filter) object or an array of [`Filter`](#Filter) objects to generate multiple filter components.

#### Example

<TableContainer minHeight="380">
    filter={true}
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

```html
<active-table filter="true"></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  filter="true"
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

## Types

Object types for filter:

### `Filter` {#Filter}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`caseButton?: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`dropdown?: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`defaultColumnHeaderName?: string`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`placeholderTemplate?: string`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`styles?: FilterStyles`](#FilterStyles), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`position?: OuterContentPosition`](/docs/sharedTypes#OuterContentPosition), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`order?: number` <br />
- Default: {<br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_caseButton: true_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_dropdown: true_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_placeholderTemplate: "Filter {headerName}..."_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_position: "top-right"_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_order: 1_ <br />

Custom settings for a row filter input component. <br />
`caseButton` is used to toggle the visibility of a button that controls if row filtering is case sensitive. <br />
`dropdown` is used to toggle the visibility of a button that is used to display the column selection dropdown. <br />
`defaultColumnHeaderName` is the header name of the column that the filter will be targeting by default. If not set, it will use the first data column on the left. <br />
`placeholderTemplate` is a special template string that is used to control the input element's placeholder text. Inside the template - include the following substring
to denote where the column name will be set: _"{headerName}"_. If your template string is _"Filter {headerName}"_ and the target column's header name is _"Brand"_,
the placeholder text will be _"Filter Brand"_. <br />
`styles` is used to style the various elements inside the filter component. <br />
`position` is used to set the location of the filter component. <br />
`order` is the order of the component when other ones are also placed in the same position.

#### Example

<TableContainer minHeight="509">
    filter={[
      {
        caseButton: false,
        dropdown: false,
        defaultColumnHeaderName: 'Mass',
        placeholderTemplate: 'Filter by {headerName}',
        position: 'top-left',
        order: 1,
      },
      {
        caseButton: true,
        dropdown: true,
        defaultColumnHeaderName: 'Planet',
        placeholderTemplate: '{headerName}',
        position: 'top-left',
        order: 2,
      },
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
      ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
      ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
      ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

```html
<active-table
  filter='[
    {
      "caseButton": false,
      "dropdown": false,
      "defaultColumnHeaderName": "Mass",
      "placeholderTemplate": "Filter by {headerName}",
      "position": "top-left",
      "order": 1
    },
    {
      "caseButton": true,
      "dropdown": true,
      "defaultColumnHeaderName": "Planet",
      "placeholderTemplate": "{headerName}",
      "position": "top-left",
      "order": 2
    }
  ]'
></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  filter='[
    {
      "caseButton": false,
      "dropdown": false,
      "defaultColumnHeaderName": "Mass",
      "placeholderTemplate": "Filter by {headerName}",
      "position": "top-left",
      "order": 1
    },
    {
      "caseButton": true,
      "dropdown": true,
      "defaultColumnHeaderName": "Planet",
      "placeholderTemplate": "{headerName}",
      "position": "top-left",
      "order": 2
    }
  ]'
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
    ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
    ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
    ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

### `FilterStyles` {#FilterStyles}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`input?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`placeholderColor?: string`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`caseIcon?:` [`StatefulCSS`](/docs/sharedTypes#StatefulCSS) & {[`active?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle)}, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`dropdownIcon?:` [`StatefulCSS`](/docs/sharedTypes#StatefulCSS) & {[`active?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle)} <br />

Styling properties for a filter component. <br />
`input` defines the styling for the input element. <br />
`placeholderColor` is the color used for the placeholder text. <br />
`caseIcon` defines the styling for the various states of the element that toggles case sensitive filtering. <br />
`dropdownIcon` defines styling for the various states of the element that toggles the column selection dropdown. <br />

#### Example

<TableContainer minHeight="380">
    filter={{
      styles: {
        input: {height: '22px', fontSize: '15px', width: '150px', borderColor: '#818181', color: 'black'},
        placeholderColor: 'grey',
        caseIcon: {
          default: {color: 'grey', fontSize: '15px'},
          hover: {color: 'black'},
          click: {color: 'black'},
          active: {color: 'blue'},
        },
        dropdownIcon: {
          default: {color: 'grey', width: '18px', height: '18px'},
          hover: {color: 'black'},
          click: {color: 'black'},
          active: {color: 'blue'},
        },
      },
    }}
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

```html
<active-table
  filter='{
    "styles": {
      "input": {"height": "22px", "fontSize": "15px", "width": "150px", "borderColor": "#818181", "color": "black"},
      "placeholderColor": "grey",
      "caseIcon": {
        "default": {"color": "grey", "fontSize": "15px"},
        "hover": {"color": "black"},
        "click": {"color": "black"},
        "active": {"color": "blue"}
      },
      "dropdownIcon": {
        "default": {"color": "grey", "width": "18px", "height": "18px"},
        "hover": {"color": "black"},
        "click": {"color": "black"},
        "active": {"color": "blue"}
      }
    }
  }'
></active-table>
```

      "placeholderColor": "grey",
      "caseIcon": {
        "default": {"color": "grey", "fontSize": "15px"},

# Header

Source: https://github.com/ovidijusparsiunas/active-table/blob/main/website/docs/docs/header.mdx

sidebar_position: 4

# Header

Properties related to the header cells.

### `headerStyles` {#headerStyles}

- Type: [`HoverableStyles`](/docs/sharedTypes#HoverableStyles)
- Default: _unset_

Styling details for the header elements in default and mouse hover states. To prevent the frame
component (index and add new column) from inheriting the header style, set `inheritHeaderColors` property
in [`frameComponentsStyles`](/docs/table#frameComponentsStyles) to _false_.

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    headerStyles={{
      default: {
        backgroundColor: '#efefef',
        borderBottom: 'unset',
        fontWeight: '700',
        fontSize: '15px',
      },
      hoverColors: {
        backgroundColor: '#d2d2d2',
      },
    }}

```html
<active-table
  headerStyles='{
    "default": {
      "backgroundColor": "#efefef",
      "borderBottom": "unset",
      "fontWeight": "700",
      "fontSize": "15px"
    },
    "hoverColors": {
      "backgroundColor": "#d2d2d2"
    }
  }'
></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  headerStyles='{
    "default": {
      "backgroundColor": "#efefef",
      "borderBottom": "unset",
      "fontWeight": "700",
      "fontSize": "15px"
    },
    "hoverColors": {
      "backgroundColor": "#d2d2d2"
    }
  }'
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

### `isHeaderTextEditable` {#isHeaderTextEditable}

- Type: `boolean`
- Default: _true_

Controls if cell text can be edited for header cells.

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    isHeaderTextEditable={false}

```html
<active-table isHeaderTextEditable="false"></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  isHeaderTextEditable="false"
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

### `allowDuplicateHeaders` {#allowDuplicateHeaders}

- Type: `boolean`
- Default: _true_

Allows multiple columns to have the same header text. If set to _false_ and a duplicate is found the header text is defaulted to the value inside
[`defaultText`](/docs/data#defaultText).

#### Example for false

<TableContainer>
    allowDuplicateHeaders={false}
      ['Planet', 'Planet', 'Moons', 'Moons', 'Density'],

```html
<active-table allowDuplicateHeaders="false"></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  allowDuplicateHeaders="false"
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Planet", "Moons", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

### `displayHeaderIcons` {#displayHeaderIcons}

- Type: `boolean`
- Default: _true_

Displays an icon beside header text that represents the column type.

#### Example for false

<TableContainer>
    displayHeaderIcons={false}

```html
<active-table displayHeaderIcons="false"></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  displayHeaderIcons="false"
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

### `headerIconStyle` {#HeaderIconStyle}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `filterColor?: string`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `scale?`: {`x?: number`, `y?: number`}<br />
- Default: {<br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; _iconFilterColor: 'brightness(0) saturate(100%) invert(34%) sepia(0%) saturate(1075%) hue-rotate(211deg) brightness(96%) contrast(90%)'_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; _scale: {x: 1.1, y: 1.1}_<br />

Styling details for the column header icons. The color is set by using the `filterColor` property which requires
a [filter](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/filter) string (the reason for this is because the icon is an SVG element)
that can be retrieved using the [cssfilterconverter](https://cssfilterconverter.com/) tool . Use `scale` to resize the icon dimensions.

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    headerIconStyle={{
      filterColor:
        'brightness(0) saturate(100%) invert(16%) sepia(85%) saturate(1892%) hue-rotate(210deg) brightness(88%) contrast(103%)',
      scale: {x: 1.5, y: 1.5},
    }}

```html
<active-table
  headerIconStyle='{
    "filterColor": "brightness(0) saturate(100%) invert(16%) sepia(85%) saturate(1892%) hue-rotate(210deg) brightness(88%) contrast(103%)",
    "scale": {"x": 1.5, "y": 1.5}
  }'
></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  headerIconStyle='{
    "filterColor": "brightness(0) saturate(100%) invert(16%) sepia(85%) saturate(1892%) hue-rotate(210deg) brightness(88%) contrast(103%)",
    "scale": {"x": 1.5, "y": 1.5}
  }'
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

### `stickyHeader` {#stickyHeader}

- Type: `boolean`
- Default: _false_ or if [`overflow`](/docs/table#overflow) property is defined set to _true_

Header row will remain at the top of the table when there is overflow in the table or a parent element.

#### Example

<TableContainer customStyle={{maxHeight: '200px', overflow: 'auto'}}>
    stickyHeader={true}
    tableStyle={{width: '97%', boxShadow: 'rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px', borderRadius: '2px'}}

```html
<active-table stickyHeader="true"></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<div style="maxHeight: 200px; overflow: auto">
  <active-table
    stickyHeader="true"
    data='[
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
    tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
  ></active-table>
</div>
```

:::note
The scrollbar in this example is located on the parent div element, however when using the [`overflow`](/docs/table#overflow) property
it would be placed directly on the actual table component.

### `dataStartsAtHeader` {#dataStartsAtHeader}

- Type: `boolean`
- Default: _false_

Starts the index column count at header row and if [`pagination`](/docs/pagination) is used the header row will not be displayed in pages after the first.

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    dataStartsAtHeader={'true'}

```html
<active-table dataStartsAtHeader="true"></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  dataStartsAtHeader="true"
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

# Installation

Source: https://github.com/ovidijusparsiunas/active-table/blob/main/website/docs/docs/installation.mdx

sidebar_position: 1

# Installation

Install the component via [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/):

```bash
npm install active-table
```

For React, install the following instead: <br />

```bash
npm install active-table-react
```

Access the component via CDN:

```
https://unpkg.com/active-table@1.1.8/dist/activeTable.bundle.js
```

---

# Introduction

Source: https://github.com/ovidijusparsiunas/active-table/blob/main/website/docs/docs/introduction.mdx

sidebar_position: 0

# Introduction

<h2 id="#heading-id">
  Active Table is a web component built with a focus on delivering the best editable table experience possible.
</h2>

It is a one stop shop for editable data features that are backed by an extensive API to allow you to customize a table that fits your needs.

### Vision

Building a table structure with customizable editability features is no easy feat. This is a challenge that we took on with full force, delivering a table
component that is a power-house of editability and an exposé of customization.

No two tables are ever the same, some require categorical data, some only allow partial augmentation, whilst others allow numerical data exclusively.
The list of possible requirements is virtually endless, we get it and we are here for you. Whatever the requirements are the API that we are building hopes to help
shape the table you need. This is why Active Table is continuously enriched with new features that aim to encapsulate your requirements.

Developer experience is paramount to our success, this is why the component is shipped in a cross-framework plug and play package for you to have it running in seconds!
It is also no secret that the addition of more features can increase the API complexity - this is why we pay extra care and listen to our users' feedback to present
an interface that provides the most intuitive and seamless experience when working with Active Table.

### Open source

Open source is at the heart of what we do. Active Table is built by the community - for the community. All contributions to this [**project**](https://github.com/OvidijusParsiunas/active-table) are welcome!

If you have any suggestions for enhancements, ideas on how to take the project further or have discovered a bug, do not hesitate to create a new [**issue ticket**](https://github.com/OvidijusParsiunas/active-table/issues/new/choose) and we will look into it as soon as possible!

---

# Methods

Source: https://github.com/ovidijusparsiunas/active-table/blob/main/website/docs/docs/methods.mdx

sidebar_position: 11

# Methods

Method properties that can be called directly on the Active Table element.

:::info
Make sure the Active Table component has been fully rendered on the DOM before using these.

### `getData` {#getData}

- Type: `() => (string|number)[][]`

Returns current table contents 2D array.

#### Example

import TableContainerProgrammaticUpdates from '@site/src/components/table/tableContainerProgrammaticUpdates';
import TableContainerMethods from '@site/src/components/table/tableContainerMethods';

<BrowserOnly>{() => require('@site/src/components/externalModules/externalModules').importXLSX()}</BrowserOnly>

<TableContainerMethods propertyName={"getData"}>
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

</TableContainerMethods>

<TabItem value="js" label="Code">

```javascript
tableElementRef.getData();
```

### `getColumnsDetails` {#getColumnsDetails}

- Type: [`() => ColumnsDetails`](/docs/sharedTypes#ColumnsDetails)

Returns details related to existing columns - `width`, `typeName` and `cellDropdownItems` (if the column type contains a dropdown). This is particularly useful if the user has made changes to columns and you want to recreate them
in the next session on the initial load.

#### Example

<TableContainerMethods propertyName={"getColumnsDetails"}>
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

</TableContainerMethods>

<TabItem value="js" label="Code">

```javascript
tableElementRef.getColumnsDetails();
```

### `updateCell` {#updateCell}

- Type: `(update: CellDetails) => void`

#### `CellDetails` {#CellDetails}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `newText:` `string | number`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `rowIndex: number`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `columnIndex: number` <br />

Update cell text programmatically. Both `rowIndex` and `columnIndex` start at _0_ where it is the header row for
`rowIndex` and the left-most column for `columnIndex`.

#### Example

<TableContainerProgrammaticUpdates>
      ['Name', 'CPU', 'Memory', 'Disk', 'Network'],
      ['Chrome', '4.5%', '1400MB', '0.2MB/s', '1.2Mbps'],
      ['Firefox', '2.5%', '800MB', '0.1MB/s', '0.5Mbps'],
      ['Edge', '5.5%', '1000MB', '1.4MB/s', '0.7Mbps'],
      ['Safari', '1.5%', '1200MB', '1.2MB/s', '0.2Mbps'],
      ['Opera', '3.5%', '400MB', '0.8MB/s', '0.5Mbps'],
</TableContainerProgrammaticUpdates>

```javascript
tableElementRef.updateCell({newText: 'sample text', rowIndex: 1, columnIndex: 1});
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  id="active-table"
  data='[
    ["Name", "CPU", "Memory", "Disk", "Network"],
    ["Chrome", "4.5%", "1400MB", "0.2MB/s", "1.2Mbps"],
    ["Firefox", "2.5%", "800MB", "0.1MB/s", "0.5Mbps"],
    ["Edge", "5.5%", "1000MB", "1.4MB/s", "0.7Mbps"],
    ["Safari", "1.5%", "1200MB", "1.2MB/s", "0.2Mbps"],
    ["Opera", "3.5%", "400MB", "0.8MB/s", "0.5Mbps"]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>

<script>
  function updateCell(tableElement) {
    if (!tableElement?.isConnected) return;
    setTimeout(() => {
      const rowIndex = Math.floor(Math.random() * 5 + 1);
      const columnIndex = Math.floor(Math.random() * 5 + 1);
      let newText = '';
      if (columnIndex === 1) {
        newText = `${Math.round(Math.random() * 20 * 10) / 10}%`;
      } else if (columnIndex === 2) {
        newText = `${Math.round(Math.random() * 1500 * 10) / 10}MB`;
      } else if (columnIndex === 3) {
        newText = `${Math.round(Math.random() * 1.5 * 10) / 10}MB/s`;
      } else {
        newText = `${Math.round(Math.random() * 1.5 * 10) / 10}Mbps`;
      }
      tableElement.updateCell({newText, rowIndex, columnIndex});
      updateCell(tableElement);
    }, 100);
  }
  const tableElementRef = document.getElementById('active-table');
  updateCell(tableElementRef);
</script>
```

### `updateStructure` {#updateStructure}

- Type: [`(update: StructureDetails) => void`](#StructureDetails)

#### `StructureDetails` {#StructureDetails}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `structure:` `"row"` | `"column"`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `isInsert: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `index: number`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `data?: (string|number)[]` <br />

Programmatically insert/remove rows/columns. <br />
`structure` defines whether the structure type is for a _"row"_ or a _"column"_. <br />
`isInsert` sets the update behaviour; _true_ will create a new structure, _false_ will remove an existing one. <br />
`index` is the row/column index. When adding a new structure, a value of _-1_ will append it to the end of the table. <br />
`data` defines the new cells' content. If not defined and the update is for an insert, this will be populated with [`defaultText`](/docs/data#defaultText).

#### Example

<TableContainerMethods propertyName={"updateStructure"} displayResults={false} argument={{structure: 'row', isInsert: true, index: -1, data: ['New Planet', '12345', '500', '10', '357']}}>
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

</TableContainerMethods>

<TabItem value="js" label="Code">

```javascript
tableElementRef.updateStructure({
  structure: 'row',
  isInsert: true,
  index: -1,
  data: ['New Planet', '12345', '500', '10', '357'],
});
```

### `updateData` {#updateData}

- Type: `(data: (number | string)[][]) => void`

Programmatically reset table data using the new data iside the `data` argument. <br />

#### Example

<TableContainerMethods propertyName={"updateData"} displayResults={false} argument={[
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ['Mercury', 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
      ['Venus', 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
      ['Uranus', 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
      ['Pluto', 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
      ['Moon', 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340]]}>
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

</TableContainerMethods>

<TabItem value="js" label="Code">

```javascript
tableElementRef.updateData([
  ['Planet', 'Diameter', 'Mass', 'Moons', 'Density'],
  ['Mercury', 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
  ['Venus', 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
  ['Uranus', 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
  ['Pluto', 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
  ['Moon', 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],
]);
```

### `importFile` {#importFile}

- Type: [`(options?: ImportOptions) => void`](/docs/files#ImportOptions)
- Default: _({formats: ["csv"]}) => void_

Opens up a file browser window to select a file and import its data. You can optionally pass an [`options`](/docs/files#ImportOptions)
object to define the allowed file formats and what they will overwrite. For browser security reasons - this method can ONLY be activated
through user actions, such as a click of a button.

#### Example

<TableContainerMethods propertyName={"importFile"} displayResults={false}>
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

</TableContainerMethods>

<TabItem value="js" label="Code">

```javascript
tableElementRef.importFile();
```

:::info
`csv` files are supported natively, however if you want to import any of the other file formats - you will need to add the [`xlsx`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/xlsx) module
into your project. Please see examples [here](../../examples/files).

### `exportFile` {#exportFile}

- Type: [`(options?: ExportSingleFile) => void`](#ExportSingleFile)
- Default: _({fileName: "table_data", format: "csv"}) => void_

#### `ExportSingleFile` {#ExportSingleFile}

- Type: {`fileName?: string`, [`format?: FileFormat`](/docs/files#FileFormat)}

Exports existing table data into a file. You can optionally pass a [`ExportSingleFile`](#ExportSingleFile) object
to define the exported file's name and its format.

#### Example

<TableContainerMethods propertyName={"exportFile"} displayResults={false}>
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

</TableContainerMethods>

<TabItem value="js" label="Code">

```javascript
tableElementRef.exportFile();
```

:::info
`csv` files are supported natively, however if you want to export any of the other file formats - you will need to add the [`xlsx`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/xlsx) module
into your project. Please see examples [here](../../examples/files).

# Pagination

Source: https://github.com/ovidijusparsiunas/active-table/blob/main/website/docs/docs/pagination.mdx

sidebar_position: 8

# Pagination

Divides table rows into a series of pages.

### `pagination` {#pagination}

- Type: `boolean` | {<br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`rowsPerPage?: number`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`rowsPerPageSelect?: boolean|RowsPerPageSelect`](#RowsPerPageSelect), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`maxNumberOfVisiblePageButtons?: number`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`displayPrevNext?: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`displayFirstLast?: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`displayNumberOfVisibleRows?: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`styles?: PaginationStyle`](#PaginationStyle), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`positions?: PaginationPositions`](#PaginationPositions) <br />
- Default: {<br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_rowsPerPage: 10_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_rowsPerPageSelect: true_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_maxNumberOfVisiblePageButtons: 8_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_displayPrevNext: true_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_displayFirstLast: true_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_displayNumberOfVisibleRows: true_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_positions: refer to the PaginationPositions type_ <br />

`rowsPerPage` is the number of maximum data rows that can be displayed in a single page. <br />
`rowsPerPageSelect` facilitates a `rowsPerPage` selection button that opens up a dropdown containing a number of options that the user can select
to change `rowsPerPage`. <br />
`maxNumberOfVisiblePageButtons` is the maximum number of page (number) buttons that are visible, the rest will be hidden. <br />
`displayPrevNext` defines whether the previous and next page buttons are displayed. <br />
`displayFirstLast` defines whether the first and last page buttons are displayed. <br />
`displayNumberOfVisibleRows` displays information on the index of currently visible rows out of the total number of rows in the table. E.g. _1-5 of 20_. <br />
`styles` defines the styling properties of pagination components. <br />
`positions` defines pagination components positions. <br />

#### Example

<TableContainer minHeight="602">
    pagination={true}
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
      ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
      ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
      ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
      ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
      ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
      ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
      ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
      ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
      ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
      ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

```html
<active-table pagination="true"></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  pagination="true"
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
    ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
    ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
    ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
    ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
    ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
    ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
    ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
    ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
    ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
    ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>

## Types

Object types for properties inside [`pagination`](#pagination):

### `RowsPerPageSelect` {#RowsPerPageSelect}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`prefixText?: string`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`options?: (number | "all" | "All" )[]` <br />
- Default: {<br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_prefixText: "Rows per page"_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_options: [10, 25, 50, "All"]_ <br />

Custom settings for the `rowsPerPageSelect` property. <br />
`prefixText` is the text that is displayed before the button. <br />
`options` is the array of options that are displayed in the dropdown. `"all"|"All"` option displays all of the table's rows within one page.
If the defined `rowsPerPage` value (in [`pagination`](#pagination) object) is not in the options array, it will be added to it automatically. <br />

#### Example

<TableContainer minHeight="388">
    pagination={{
      "rowsPerPageSelect": {"prefixText": "Number of rows:", "options": [10, 20, 30, "All"]},
      "rowsPerPage": 5
    }}
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],

      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
      ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
      ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
      ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
      ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
      ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],

    "rowsPerPage": 5

### `PaginationStyle` {#PaginationStyle}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`rowsPerPageSelect?: RowsPerPageOptionsStyle`](#RowsPerPageOptionsStyle), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`numberOfVisibleRows?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`pageButtons?: PageButtonStyle`](#PageButtonStyle) <br />

Styling properties of pagination components. <br />
`rowsPerPageSelect` defines styling properties for the rowsPerPage button container and its dropdown.
`numberOfVisibleRows` defines styling properties for the number of visible rows text. <br />
`pageButtons` defines styling properties for the page/previous/next/first/last buttons. <br />

#### Example

<TableContainer minHeight="388">
    pagination={{
      "styles": {
        "rowsPerPageSelect": {
          "prefixText": {"color": "#174a76"},
          "buttonText": {"default":{"color": "#174a76"}},
          "buttonArrow": {"default":{"filter": "brightness(0) saturate(100%) invert(22%) sepia(77%) saturate(620%) hue-rotate(168deg) brightness(96%) contrast(95%)"}}
        },
        "numberOfVisibleRows": {"color": "#174a76"},
        "pageButtons": {
          "buttons": {
            "default": {"color": "steelblue", "stroke": "steelblue", "border":"1px solid #dedede", "borderRight": "unset"}
          },
          "activeButton": {"default": {"backgroundColor": "steelblue", "color": "white", "border":"1px solid steelblue"}},
          "firstVisibleButtonOverride": {"borderTopLeftRadius": "2px", "borderBottomLeftRadius": "2px"},
          "lastVisibleButtonOverride": {"borderRight": "1px solid #dedede", "borderTopRightRadius": "2px", "borderBottomRightRadius": "2px"},
          "activeButtonPrecedence": true
      }},
      "rowsPerPage": 5
    }}
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],

:::tip
When number of visible rows text contains digits that are in the 100s+, it is advisable to set `numberOfVisibleRows` with a `minWidth` value that is higher than
_32px_ to stop side components from moving when its digits change.

### `RowsPerPageOptionsStyle` {#RowsPerPageOptionsStyle}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`container?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`prefixText?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`button?: StatefulCSS`](/docs/sharedTypes#StatefulCSS), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`buttonText?: StatefulCSS`](/docs/sharedTypes#StatefulCSS), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`buttonArrow?: StatefulCSS`](/docs/sharedTypes#StatefulCSS) <br />

Styling properties for the rows per page component elements. `container` is the parent element that encapsulates all of the rows per page elements.

:::info
Because `buttonArrow` is an svg icon - its color is set via _filter_ property. You can use the [cssfilterconverter](https://cssfilterconverter.com/) tool to generate its values.

### `PageButtonStyle` {#PageButtonStyle}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`container?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`buttons?: StatefulCSS`](/docs/sharedTypes#StatefulCSS), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`activeButton?: StatefulCSS`](/docs/sharedTypes#StatefulCSS), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`activeButtonPrecedence?: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`disabledButtons?: StatefulCSS`](/docs/sharedTypes#StatefulCSS), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`actionButtons?: ActionButtonStyle`](#ActionButtonStyle), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`firstVisibleButtonOverride?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`lastVisibleButtonOverride?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle) <br />
- Default: {<br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_activeButtonPrecedence: false_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_actionButtons: uses the buttons property style_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_disabledButtons: partially uses the buttons property style_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_actionButtons: partially uses the buttons property style_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_firstVisibleButtonOverride: {borderLeft: '1px solid #0000004d', borderTopLeftRadius: '2px', borderBottomLeftRadius: '2px'}_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_lastVisibleButtonOverride: {borderRight: '1px solid #0000004d', borderTopRightRadius: '2px', borderBottomRightRadius: '2px'}_ <br />

Styling properties for the page buttons component elements. <br />
`container` is the parent element that encapsulates all of the buttons. <br />
`buttons` is used to styles the buttons with numbers, however its properties are also reused by `actionButtons`, `disabledButtons` and `actionButtons`. Use the _TIPs_ below to help
styles them correctly. <br />
`activeButton` is the button with the currently active page number. <br />
`activeButtonPrecedence` denotes whether its border properties overcomes the sibling border properties (except radius). <br />
`disabledButtons` are buttons that have no events and cannot be clicked. E.g. buttons when there are no data rows or
action buttons when the currently active page number is either the first or the last. <br />
`actionButtons` are buttons that change the currently active page number to next, previous, first and last. <br />
`firstVisibleButtonOverride` and `lastVisibleButtonOverride` are used for overriding the properties of first or last buttons within the container, e.g. setting
the border radius or setting the opposite side border property when the `buttons` styles border properties are set for the other.
Eg. when
default properties are _"border": "1px solid #dedede", "borderRight": "unset"_, set `lastVisibleButtonOverride` with \_"borderLeft":"1px solid #dedede"\_
as otherwise the last button is not going to have a border on the right.

#### Example

<TableContainer minHeight="388">
    pagination={{
      "styles": {
        "pageButtons": {
          "buttons": {
            "default": {
              "color": "#3682ec", "stroke": "#3682ec", "border":"1px solid #dedede", "borderRight": "unset", "minWidth": "30px"
          }},
          "activeButton": {"default": {"backgroundColor": "#3682ec", "color": "white", "border":"1px solid #3682ec"}},
          "firstVisibleButtonOverride": {"borderTopLeftRadius": "5px", "borderBottomLeftRadius": "5px"},
          "lastVisibleButtonOverride": {"borderRight": "1px solid #dedede", "borderTopRightRadius": "5px", "borderBottomRightRadius": "5px"},
          "activeButtonPrecedence": true
      }},
      "rowsPerPage": 5
    }}
      ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
      ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
      ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
      ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
      ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
      ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
      ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
      ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
      ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
      ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
      ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],
      ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
      ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
      ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
      ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

    ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
    ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
    ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
    ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
    ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
    ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
    ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
    ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

:::tip
When setting button widths, use `minWidth` instead of `width` to override the defaults and it is additionally useful to automatically expand
the button widths in situations when their numbers contain multiple digits that surpass the currently defined width dimensions.

:::tip
When buttons are grouped next to each other and they have borders, set `borderRight` to _"unset"_ in the `buttons` property to create an appearance of a thin border.
When doing this you will additionally need to set `borderLeft` with a pixel value on `lastVisibleButtonOverride` as the rightmost button would not have a right border.

:::info
When using `activeButtonPrecedence` with thin `buttons` borders (in the tip above), make sure to set `borderRight` to _"unset"_ and not _"borderLeft"_ as the css selector limitations only allow
the active button to unset the left border of the right sibling and not the left.

### `ActionButtonStyle` {#ActionButtonStyle}

- Type: {[`StatefulCSS`](/docs/sharedTypes#StatefulCSS) & <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`previousText?: string`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`nextText?: string`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`firstText?: string`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`lastText?: string` <br />

Styling for action buttons that facilitates the definition of styles for various mouse states and the text that is displayed in each one.

### `PaginationPositions` {#PaginationPositions}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`pageButtons?: PaginationPosition`](#PaginationPosition), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`numberOfVisibleRows?: PaginationPosition`](#PaginationPosition), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`rowsPerPageSelect?: PaginationPosition`](#PaginationPosition) <br />
- Default: {<br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_pageButtons: {position: "bottom-right", "order": 3}_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_numberOfVisibleRows: {position: "bottom-right", "order": 2}_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_rowsPerPageSelect: {position: "bottom-right", "order": 1}_ <br />

Positions for pagination components.

#### `PaginationPosition` {#PaginationPosition}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[`position?: OuterContentPosition`](/docs/sharedTypes#OuterContentPosition), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`order?: number` <br />
- Default: {<br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_position: "bottom-right"_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;_order: 1_ <br />

Object defining position properties for a pagination component. `order` is the order of the component when other ones are also placed in the same position.

      ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
      ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
      ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
      ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
      ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
      ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340]]}
    tableStyle={{"width":"100%", "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}}

```html

  pagination='{
    "styles": {
      "pageButtons": {
        "buttons": {

          "hover": {"backgroundColor":"white"}},

        "activeButtonPrecedence": true

    "rowsPerPageSelect": false,
    "displayNumberOfVisibleRows": false,
    "positions": {"pageButtons": {"position": "bottom-center"}},
    "rowsPerPage": 2
  }'
></active-table>
```

# Row

Source: https://github.com/ovidijusparsiunas/active-table/blob/main/website/docs/docs/row.mdx

sidebar_position: 5

# Row

Properties related to table rows.

### `rowHoverStyles` {#rowHoverStyles}

- Type: {[`style: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle), `header?: boolean`, `addNewRowButton?: boolean`}
- Default: _unset_, but if _style_ is set then _header_ and _addNewRowButton_ are _true_

Custom styling for row mouse hover. `header` property denotes if `style` can be applied to the header row
and `addNewRowButton` denotes if `style` can be applied to the add new row button if it is displayed.

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    rowHoverStyles={{style: {backgroundColor: '#d6d6d630', transitionDuration: '0.05s'}}}

```html
<active-table rowHoverStyles='{"style":{"backgroundColor": "#d6d6d630", "transitionDuration": "0.05s"}}'></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  rowHoverStyles='{"style":{"backgroundColor": "#d6d6d630", "transitionDuration": "0.05s"}}'
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

:::caution
Custom default cell styles will override this property's styling. Additionally, using this property unsets the header (if set to _true_)
and [`frameComponentsStyles`](/docs/table#frameComponentsStyles) hover color properties.

### `stripedRows` {#stripedRows}

- Type: `boolean` | { [`odd?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle), [`even?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle) }
- Default: _false_, but if set to _true_ then _even_ is _{backgroundColor: ''}_ and _odd_ is _{backgroundColor: '#dcdcdc7a'}}_

Stripe based styling for rows.

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    stripedRows={{odd: {backgroundColor: ''}, even: {backgroundColor: '#ebebeb7a'}}}
    cellStyle={{borderBottom: 'unset'}}

```html
<active-table stripedRows='{"odd": {"backgroundColor": ""}, "even": {"backgroundColor": "#ebebeb7a"}}'></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  stripedRows='{"odd": {"backgroundColor": ""}, "even": {"backgroundColor": "#ebebeb7a"}}'
  cellStyle='{"borderBottom": "unset"}'
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

:::info
Using this property unsets the default header and [`frameComponentsStyles`](/docs/table#frameComponentsStyles) hover color properties.
If the component is set with a [`cellStyle`](/docs/data#cellStyle) property - this will be overriden.

### `rowDropdown` {#rowDropdown}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; [`displaySettings: DropdownDisplaySettings`](/docs/sharedTypes#DropdownDisplaySettings), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `isInsertUpAvailable?: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `isInsertDownAvailable?: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `isMoveAvailable?: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `isDeleteAvailable?: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `canEditHeaderRow?: boolean` <br />
- Default: {<br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; _displaySettings: {isAvailable: true, openMethod: {cellClick: true}}_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; _isInsertUpAvailable: true_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; _isInsertDownAvailable: true_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; _isMoveAvailable: true_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; _isDeleteAvailable: true_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; _canEditHeaderRow: true_ <br />

Row dropdown settings. If [`displaySettings`](/docs/sharedTypes#DropdownDisplaySettings) object's `openMethod` property has `cellClick` set to _true_ - simply click on the left-most
row cell to open the dropdown. If `openMethod` is `overlayClick` - hover over the left-most cell and click on the overlay. <br />
The `canEditHeaderRow` property denotes whether this dropdown can be used to change the header row e.g. move or delete it, therefore
it does not open on header row when set to _false_.

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    rowDropdown={{displaySettings: {isAvailable: true, openMethod: {overlayClick: true}}, canEditHeaderRow: false}}
    columnDropdown={{displaySettings: {isAvailable: true, openMethod: {overlayClick: true}}}}

```html
<active-table
  rowDropdown='{"displaySettings":{"isAvailable": true, "openMethod": {"overlayClick": true}}, "canEditHeaderRow": false}'
></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  rowDropdown='{"displaySettings":{"isAvailable": true, "openMethod": {"overlayClick": true}}, "canEditHeaderRow": false}'
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px", "borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

### `maxRows` {#maxRows}

- Type: `number`
- Default: _unset_

Maximum number of rows allowed (including header row).

#### Example

<TableContainer minHeight="215">
    maxRows={4}

```html
<active-table maxRows="4"></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  maxRows="4"
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

### `dragRows` {#dragRows}

- Type: `boolean`
- Default: _true_

Toggles the ability to change row positions by dragging index column cells or their overlays with your mouse. <br />

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    dragRows={true}

```html
<active-table dragRows="true"></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  dragRows="true"
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

:::note
Dragging rows is not available when using [`pagination`](/docs/pagination) or [`filter`](/docs/filter) features.

### `displayAddNewRow` {#displayAddNewRow}

- Type: `boolean`
- Default: _true_

A toggle for a clickable '+ New' row at the bottom of the table which is used to add new empty rows. <br />
You can set the add new row style via [`frameComponentsStyles`](/docs/table#frameComponentsStyles).

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    displayAddNewRow={true}

```html
<active-table displayAddNewRow="true"></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  displayAddNewRow="true"
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

# Shared types

Source: https://github.com/ovidijusparsiunas/active-table/blob/main/website/docs/docs/sharedTypes.mdx

sidebar_position: 13

# Shared types

Object types that are shared by top level properties.

### `DropdownDisplaySettings` {#DropdownDisplaySettings}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `isAvailable?: boolean`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; [`overlayStyles?: DropdownCellOverlayStyle`](#DropdownCellOverlayStyle), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `openMethod?`: { `cellClick?: boolean`, `overlayClick?: boolean` } <br />
- Default: {<br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; _isAvailable: true_, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; _openMethod_: { _cellClick: true_ } <br />

Custom styling for row and column dropdowns. <br />
`isAvailable` determines if the dropdown is is available/displayed. <br />
`overlayStyles` property is only applicable if `overlayClick` is set to _true_ and is used to style the background color
for default and mouse hover states.<br />
`openMethod` is used to define the method for opening the dropdown. Either by clicking a cell via `cellClick` or hovering over the cell
and clicking on the overlay via `overlayClick`.

#### `DropdownCellOverlayStyle` {#DropdownCellOverlayStyle}

- Type: { `default?`: { `backgroundColor: string` }, `hover?`: { `backgroundColor: string` } }

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    rowDropdown={{
      displaySettings: {
        openMethod: {overlayClick: true},
      },
    }}
    columnDropdown={{
      displaySettings: {
        openMethod: {overlayClick: true},
        overlayStyles: {default: {backgroundColor: 'grey'}, hover: {backgroundColor: 'blue'}},
      },
    }}

```html
<active-table
  rowDropdown='{"displaySettings": {
    "openMethod": {"overlayClick": true }}}'
  columnDropdown='{"displaySettings": {
    "openMethod": {"overlayClick": true }, "overlayStyles": {"default": {"backgroundColor": "grey"}, "hover": {"backgroundColor": "blue"}}}}'
></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  rowDropdown='{"displaySettings": {
    "openMethod": {"overlayClick": true }}}'
  columnDropdown='{"displaySettings": {
    "openMethod": {"overlayClick": true }, "overlayStyles": {"default": {"backgroundColor": "grey"}, "hover": {"backgroundColor": "blue"}}}}'
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

### `CSSStyle` {#CSSStyle}

- Type: [`CSSStyleDeclaration`](https://webplatform.github.io/docs/css/cssom/CSSStyleDeclaration/CSSStyleDeclaration/)

Object containing all properties defined in the CSSStyleDeclaration [`specification`](https://webplatform.github.io/docs/css/cssom/CSSStyleDeclaration/CSSStyleDeclaration/)
as optionals. A TypeScript example can be found in this [link](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript-DOM-lib-generator/blob/bf671e99615b06404db7a89fa9ae05bf14a8e47c/baselines/dom.generated.d.ts#L2737).

### `HoverableStyles` {#HoverableStyles}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; [`default?: NoDimensionCSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#NoDimensionCSSStyle), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `hoverColors?`: {`backgroundColor?: string`, `color?: string`}<br />
- Default: _unset_

Styling details for when an element is in default state and when it is hovered with a mouse. `hoverColors` object only accepts
`backgroundColor` and `color` properties.

### `StatefulCSS` {#StatefulCSS}

- Type: {[`default?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle), [`hover?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle), [`click?: CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle)}

Object defining styling properties for different mouse states on the element.

### `NoDimensionCSSStyle` {#NoDimensionCSSStyle}

- Type: { [`CSSStyle`](#CSSStyle) & `!width` & `!minWidth` & `!maxWidth` & `!height` & `!minHeight` & `!maxHeight` }

Object containing all [`CSSStyle`](#CSSStyle) properties except `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `height`, `minHeight` and `maxHeight`.

### `ColumnsDetails` {#ColumnsDetails}

- Type: { <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`width: number`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`typeName: string`, <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;`cellDropdownItems?: {name: string; backgroundColor?: string}[]` <br />
  }[]

The array elements represent each column in order from left to right. <br />
`width` is the column width in pixels. <br />
`typeName` is the name of the currently active type on the column. <br />
`cellDropdownItems` contains details about the available cell dropdown items if the active column type is using a [`dropdown`](/docs/column#CellDropdown)
(backgroundColor only for label types). <br />

### `OuterContentPosition` {#OuterContentPosition}

- Type: `"top-left"` | `"top-center"` | `"top-right"` | `"bottom-left"` | `"bottom-center"` | `"bottom-right"`

Position for a component either above the table (_top_) or below it (_bottom_).

---

# Table

Source: https://github.com/ovidijusparsiunas/active-table/blob/main/website/docs/docs/table.mdx

sidebar_position: 2

# Table

Properties related to table container.

### `tableStyle` {#tableStyle}

- Type: [`CSSStyle`](/docs/sharedTypes#CSSStyle)

Object containing CSS styling properties for the table element. <br />

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    tableStyle={{
      borderRadius: '10px',
      boxShadow: 'rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px',
      width: '100%',
    }}

```html
<active-table
  tableStyle='{
    "borderRadius": "10px",
    "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px",
    "width":"100%"
  }'
></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  tableStyle='{
    "borderRadius": "10px",
    "boxShadow": "rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px",
    "width":"100%"
  }'
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons","Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
></active-table>
```

:::tip
When table `width` needs to _inherit_ the parent element width, set `width` to 100% as displayed in the example.
:::note
`minWidth`, `height`, `minHeight`, `maxHeight` properties are not supported.

### `overflow` {#overflow}

- Type: { `maxWidth?: string`, `maxHeight?: string` }
- Default: _unset_

A scrollbar is introduced on the table if either of the specified dimensions are exceeded. The use of this object automatically sets
[`stickyHeader`](/docs/header#stickyHeader) to _true_ which can be set back to _false_ if required.

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    overflow={{maxHeight: '298px', maxWidth: '100%'}}
    tableStyle={{
      boxShadow: 'rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px',
      width: '1000px',
    }}
      ['Mercury', 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
      ['Venus', 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
      ['Uranus', 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
      ['Pluto', 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
      ['Moon', 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],

```html
<active-table overflow='{"maxHeight": "298px", "maxWidth": "100%"}' tableStyle='{"width":"1000px"}'></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  overflow='{"maxHeight": "298px", "maxWidth": "100%"}'
  tableStyle='{"width":"1000px"}'
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
    ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
    ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
    ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
    ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
    ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340]]'
></active-table>
```

### `frameComponentsStyles` {#frameComponentsStyles}

  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; [`styles?: HoverableStyles`](/docs/sharedTypes#HoverableStyles), <br />
  &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `inheritHeaderColors?: boolean` <br />
- Default: _{ inheritHeaderColors: true }_

Frame components are the index column, add new column and the add new row. This property is used to set their styling. <br />
The `styles` property defines components' styling for varying mouse states. <br />
`inheritHeaderColors` is used to toggle whether the header cells of the index column and the add new column would inherit the header
row's `backgroundColor` and text `color`.

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    frameComponentsStyles={{
      styles: {
        default: {backgroundColor: '#f5f5f5'},
        hoverColors: {backgroundColor: '#dedede'},
      },
      inheritHeaderColors: false,
    }}

```html
<active-table
  frameComponentsStyles='{
    "styles": {
      "default": {"backgroundColor": "#f5f5f5"},
      "hoverColors": {"backgroundColor": "#dedede"}},
    "inheritHeaderColors": false
  }'
></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  frameComponentsStyles='{
    "styles": {
      "default": {"backgroundColor": "#f5f5f5"},
      "hoverColors": {"backgroundColor": "#dedede"}},
    "inheritHeaderColors": false
  }'
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

### `enterKeyMoveDown` {#enterKeyMoveDown}

- Type: `boolean`
- Default: _false_

When the user presses the ENTER key, the cursor focus is moved to the cell below.

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    enterKeyMoveDown={true}

```html
<active-table enterKeyMoveDown="true"></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  enterKeyMoveDown="true"
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638]]'
  tableStyle='{"borderRadius":"2px"}'
></active-table>
```

:::caution
The autofocus does not work in the Safari browser.

### `auxiliaryStyle` {#auxiliaryStyle}

- Type: `string`

This is primarily used to configure [`Webkit CSS`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/WebKit_Extensions) which cannot be added through component's style properties. A great
example of this is the [`::-webkit-scrollbar`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/::-webkit-scrollbar) pseudo element which affects the style of the table's scrollbar.

#### Example

<TableContainer>
    overflow={{maxHeight: '298px', maxWidth: '100%'}}
    tableStyle={{
      boxShadow: 'rgb(172 172 172 / 17%) 0px 0.5px 1px 0px',
      width: '1000px',
    }}
      ['Mercury', 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
      ['Venus', 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
      ['Uranus', 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
      ['Pluto', 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
      ['Moon', 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340],
    auxiliaryStyle="
      ::-webkit-scrollbar {
        width: 10px;
        height: 10px;
      ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb {
        background-color: #54a7ff;
        border-radius: 5px;
      }"

```html
<active-table
  auxiliaryStyle="
    ::-webkit-scrollbar {
      width: 10px;
      height: 10px;
    }
    ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb {
      background-color: #54a7ff;
      border-radius: 5px;
    }"
></active-table>
```

```html
<!-- This example is for Vanilla JS and should be tailored to your framework (see Examples) -->

<active-table
  auxiliaryStyle="
    ::-webkit-scrollbar {
      width: 10px;
      height: 10px;
    }
    ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb {
      background-color: #54a7ff;
      border-radius: 5px;
    }"
  overflow='{"maxHeight": "298px", "maxWidth": "100%"}'
  tableStyle='{"width":"1000px"}'
  data='[
    ["Planet", "Diameter", "Mass", "Moons", "Density"],
    ["Earth", 12756, 5.97, 1, 5514],
    ["Mars", 6792, 0.642, 2, 3934],
    ["Jupiter", 142984, 1898, 79, 1326],
    ["Saturn", 120536, 568, 82, 687],
    ["Neptune", 49528, 102, 14, 1638],
    ["Mercury", 4879, 0.33, 0, 5429],
    ["Venus", 12104, 4.87, 0, 5243],
    ["Uranus", 51118, 86.8, 27, 1270],
    ["Pluto", 2376, 0.013, 5, 1850],
    ["Moon", 3475, 0.073, 0, 3340]]'
></active-table>
```

:::caution
If your [`Webkit CSS`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/WebKit_Extensions) properties affect element widths or heights, they may result in undesirable component dimensions.
Please use them with caution.

:::danger
[`Webkit CSS`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/WebKit_Extensions) is not standardised across all browsers, make sure to check [`browser support`](https://caniuse.com/)
for the property you are using.
